summary: The last of three Rondout Creek lights at Kingston, on the Hudson: a wooden light of 1838, a bluestone tower of 1867, and a brick light of 1915 now run as a museum reached by boat.

structures.note: First light, a wooden house with a tower on a pier on the south side of the creek (cite 1, 3)
Bluestone tower, Rondout I, attached to the keeper's dwelling; lantern removed 1916, demolished 19 May 1953; circular stone base remains (cite 1, 4)
Square cylindrical brick tower, about 48 feet, attached to the dwelling; fourth-order lantern (cite 6, 4)
Two-story brick dwelling with quarters for one keeper and family (cite 6)
Reinforced concrete pier inside a steel sheet cofferdam on wooden piles (cite 6)

access.note: Reachable only by boat. Guided tours run by the Hudson River Maritime Museum on the solar-powered Solaris, May through October (cite 2).

facts.agency: City of Kingston (owner); Hudson River Maritime Museum (operator)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The USLHS record and LighthouseFriends: 1838. The Lighthouse Directory and the Hudson River Lighthouses site: 1837. The story gives 1838 and notes 1837.
The Commissioner's report (1916) and the Lighthouse Directory give 52 feet (16 m). The USLHS record gives 40.5 feet above MHW. The story uses 52.
The 1916 report: fixed red. The Lighthouse Directory: white flash every 6 seconds. The brief's record: Fl G 4s. No Light List entry was read. The story does not state a current characteristic.
The Bulletin (1914): 23 October 1914. LighthouseFriends: 1915. The story uses the Bulletin's date.
The Commissioner's report: work started March 1914. The Hudson River Lighthouses site: construction began in 1913.
The USLHS and Directory: 250 mm (fourth order). The 1916 report: fourth-order lens, fixed red.
USLHS gives an original lens installed 1868 and a sixth-order Fresnel; LighthouseFriends gives a 300 mm Fresnel lens for the wooden light in 1855. The story does not use either.

notes_for_editor: NRHP nomination 79001640 is not digitised (NPGallery placeholder); the NRHP 1979 listing in the record is not verified. Chronicling America searches were not run for Rondout because the same loc.gov errors (HTTP 520) occurred on the other two stations; the story has no newspaper citations. The Murdock 1912 rescue (Bulletin, PDF p. 24) is OCR that garbles the keeper's name ('Jam es )lnr(\ock'). The name was checked on the page image (PDF p. 24 reads 'James Murdock, keeper of Rondout light station'), and the cumulative index (PDF p. 30) lists 'Murdock, James B., keeper Rondout light station, rescue 24, 143'. The Bulletin 1912 quote is OCR ('resc ning'), checked as printed. The 1911 Act appears on Commissioner's 1916 scan page 60 (corpus page lookup); the story cites scan page 60, not 160; the printed page number there is not confirmed. The fiscal 1916 entry on scan pages 196 (printed pp. 87-88, confirmed by the OCR page headers) is cited for the building description. LighthouseFriends' account of Catherine Murdock draws on a 1993 book and her recollections; the story paraphrases it and quotes only one short phrase from her 1907 letter as LighthouseFriends prints it. The 1878 flood is known only from LighthouseFriends; no newspaper or other report was found to confirm the Eddyville dam. The Bulletin 1914 text is OCR; the name 'Jas. B. Murdock' appears in a personnel list and 'James B. Murdock' in the rescue note. The Directory gives the current characteristic as a white flash every 6 seconds; the 1916 report gives fixed red; the brief gives Fl G 4s. No Light List entry was read, so the story gives no current characteristic. The Commissioner's report gives the visibility as nine miles without saying nautical or statute; the story keeps the report's figure. Warren Spinnenweber is named only as LighthouseFriends names him, in his public role (monitoring the light from land); the record's 'of Port Ewen' detail is left out of the story. Herman Lange and the keepers after 1960 are not in this set (none after 1954). Tour days and fees: the museum's own listing (May through October) is used; the Hudson River Lighthouses site gives a different day schedule. The story gives no tour fee.
